questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a database migration in the context of an ORM?

options.text: Define the data model schema
Transform data between applications
Manage version control of code
Optimize query performance

questions.explanation: Migrations let you evolve the database schema in sync with the application’s data model.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a backward‑compatible migration?

options.text: A migration that introduces breaking changes
A migration that can be rolled back without data loss
A migration that adds or changes columns without affecting existing data
A migration that deletes tables

questions.explanation: Backward‑compatible migrations modify the schema in ways that existing data and queries continue to work.

questions.prompt: When adding a new non‑nullable column to an existing table with data, what is the safest approach?

options.text: Add the column with a default value
Add the column without default and run an UPDATE later
Drop and recreate the table
Use a nullable column and make it non‑nullable after data is populated

questions.explanation: Adding with a default ensures every existing row gets a valid value immediately, avoiding nulls.

questions.prompt: What is a recommended strategy for safely removing a column that is still referenced by legacy code?

options.text: Drop the column immediately
Rename the column and keep it
Mark the column as deprecated in the ORM and keep it for a transition period
Delete the column and update legacy code at the same time

questions.explanation: Deprecating the column gives the legacy code time to migrate while keeping the schema stable.

questions.prompt: You need to change the data type of a column from VARCHAR to INTEGER in a table with millions of rows. Which sequence of migration steps ensures backward compatibility?

options.text: Add new integer column, copy data, drop old column, rename new column
Directly alter the column type
Drop the column, add new one, run a data migration script
Add a new integer column, leave old column, update application to use new column

questions.explanation: Adding a new column preserves the old data while the new column is populated, then you switch over safely.

questions.prompt: Which approach is best for performing a data migration that requires complex transformations on a large table without significant downtime?

options.text: Run the transformation in a single transaction
Use a background job to populate a new column gradually
Lock the table for the entire duration
Disable all writes to the table

questions.explanation: A background job processes rows incrementally, minimizing lock time and keeping the system responsive.
